title: Nvidia's Board to Investigate Reports That Jensen Huang Was Spying Target
summary: Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it has no reason to believe either national security or company secrets were compromised. The probe coincides with a congressional inquiry into the same matter.

title: How Much More AI Stock Can the Market Absorb?
summary: Tech giants, chip makers and AI cloud providers have sold or priced more than $300 billion of new stock and mandatory convertibles this year, with roughly another $100 billion in potential share sales still on tap. Most would come via at-the-market programs, including a proposed $60 billion ATM from Meta Platforms that could launch in early 2027. Volatile trading in AI stocks is testing investor appetite and the prices issuers could get.

title: Unity Draws Takeover Interest From PIF and Silver Lake Consortium
summary: An investor group including Saudi Arabia's PIF and Silver Lake has approached videogame software and ad business Unity about a buyout, which would echo the $52 billion EA acquisition by PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners in August. Unity's stock has risen from about $17 in February to $52.60, a market value near $23 billion, on growth in its AI-based ad product. Silver Lake is Unity's largest shareholder at 8%, putting it on both sides of any deal, and Unity trades at a premium to rival AppLovin, which may cap the price.

title: CoreWeave Earnings Test Neocloud Financing as Capital Tightens
summary: CoreWeave reports third-quarter results Tuesday, with analysts expecting cash burn of $10.7 billion versus $5.7 billion in the second quarter and revenue growth above 150%. Its shares have fallen about 50% in a month to $46.40, near its IPO price, and peer Iren cut its fiscal 2027 capital expenditure projections, citing tighter availability and higher cost of capital. The report will show whether management can restore investor confidence in the AI financing market.

title: Anthropic Expected to Begin IPO Roadshow Despite Market Volatility
summary: Anthropic is expected to start its institutional investor roadshow next week and appears to be on track despite questions about whether market volatility could delay the offering. The open question is what valuation it will fetch. OpenAI is also expected to host an investor call to discuss its third-quarter results.

title: A Timeline of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Suspected Spy Drama
summary: Nvidia's board has opened an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign espionage effort, following his admission of a relationship with an executive the US suspects of working for Chinese intelligence. The board is examining whether company secrets were shared. Beijing reportedly rejected the allegations, and coverage across newsletters traces how the episode unfolded over the weekend.

title: Anthropic Prepares to Push Ahead With IPO Despite Market Jitters
summary: Anthropic is preparing to proceed with its IPO even as investors grow nervous about artificial intelligence valuations and the Nvidia investigation. The move tests appetite for a flagship AI listing in volatile markets. GSMA Intelligence's weekly podcast also discussed the company's S-1 and its risk factors.

title: Enterprises Say AI Regulation Won't Stop Corporate Innovation
summary: With Democrats expected to focus on reining in AI, business technology leaders say new policies are unlikely to disrupt their technology plans. The piece, from WSJ's CIO Journal, gauges how enterprise buyers are weighing the political shift against ongoing AI investment.

title: AI Could Crack Encryption Sooner Than Quantum Computers Will
summary: AI is advancing mathematics at an unprecedented pace, including problems that have resisted solution for centuries, raising fears it could eventually find solutions to the math that underpins encrypted communications. Johns Hopkins cryptographer Matthew Green says nobody knows what is coming. The concern shifts attention from quantum computing to AI as the nearer-term threat to encryption.

title: GM to Pay $220 Million to Settle State Privacy Case Over Driver Data
summary: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million to 35 states and Washington, D.C., which accused it of selling driver data, including location and driving habits, to brokers without permission. The brokers resold the information to businesses such as insurers. In May, GM paid $12.7 million to settle a similar case with California.

title: Chainalysis Hack Exposes Data of All Users After Agentic AI-Driven Attack
summary: Chainalysis said it is still restoring systems shut down after a multifront cyberattack involving agentic AI, disclosed on Oct. 30. Names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens were exposed for all users. The company kept some systems running, including compliance transaction-monitoring products used to detect money laundering.

title: Fireworks Reveals Latest Hack Exposed Customer Data
summary: Fireworks, a startup that helps developers run and train open-source models, told large customers including Harvey of a serious recent breach that exposed some customer data. Some customers spending millions of dollars a year are considering switching providers. The incident underscores rising security risks as AI-powered breaches become more common.

title: Meta Plans Sales Team, Consulting Partnerships to Win Over Big Companies
summary: Meta is building an enterprise sales team and cultivating relationships with consulting firms to sell its AI agents and other products to businesses. The push marks a shift toward competing directly for corporate AI budgets against rivals with established enterprise channels.

title: Rakuten, AST Unveil Japan Satellite Joint Venture
summary: AST SpaceMobile and Rakuten Group formed a joint venture to build a direct-to-device network in Japan using low Earth orbit satellites. The venture is set to receive JPY148 billion in funding from the Japanese government.

title: Microsoft Walks Away From Oracle AI Rental Deal
summary: Microsoft is ending an agreement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle as it reassesses billions of dollars in cloud partnerships, according to Bloomberg. The decision points to a recalibration of how hyperscalers source AI infrastructure.

title: Alphabet Reveals $548 Million Qualcomm Stake
summary: Alphabet disclosed a $548 million stake in Qualcomm, a long-time partner that is trying to build a data centre business while its smartphone chip sales slump.

title: How Jensen Huang's Affair Spiraled Into a National Security Nightmare
summary: The WSJ details how Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's acknowledged relationship with a Singapore-based data-center executive, whom U.S. officials believe passed intelligence to China, has become a national-security issue given his lobbying of President Trump to loosen chip export controls. Trump defended Huang on Monday and said the FBI was looking into the matter, while the Commerce Department denied that it dropped a probe into Megaspeed's suspected chip diversion after outreach from an Nvidia executive. Lawmakers from both parties urged passage of AI chip export-control bills, and a House panel has asked Huang to testify later this month; Nvidia shares fell about 4% on Monday and declined further Tuesday.

title: Anthropic to Seek $1.3 Trillion Valuation in IPO
summary: Anthropic filed to sell 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each, targeting a valuation of about $1.33 trillion and raising more than $61 billion at the midpoint, with trading expected later this month. The target is below the roughly $1.5 trillion investors anticipated a week earlier, and WSJ columnist Asa Fitch argues the offering is the clearest test of whether a capital crunch in AI financing is setting in. Ahead of the listing, the company also released Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, the latter offered to select organizations with fewer safeguards for cyber and life-sciences uses.

title: A Reined In Jensen Huang Is Nvidia's Best Option
summary: Heard on the Street argues that keeping Huang but placing tighter checks on him, including national-security monitoring that is credibly independent of the CEO and possible changes to a board that has no chairman, would best serve Nvidia in the next phase of the AI boom. The Morning Download adds that Nvidia has no succession plan and that three of its 10 independent directors have served 25 years or more, compared with an average tenure under eight years at large U.S. companies. Nvidia's forward price-to-earnings ratio near 12 reflects significant investor doubt about the durability of its profits.

title: Hackers Hunt for AI's Most Valuable Commodity: Computing Power
summary: Cybercriminals are increasingly stealing API keys that grant access to AI models from labs such as Anthropic and OpenAI. Attackers use the stolen keys to run models at the victims' expense, with charges billed to the companies whose credentials were taken. The trend turns AI compute into a new category of digital asset worth targeting.

title: Silicon Valley's Data Center Hand-Wringing Begins
summary: Last week's election results, including several approved anti-data-center ballot measures, have made local opposition a serious threat to AI infrastructure plans, and some companies are now approaching governors-elect to gauge their intentions. Investor Brad Gerstner suggested that 35% of U.S. data-center projects planned for next year could be in jeopardy. Democrats expected to chair key congressional committees also plan to investigate data centers' impact on electricity prices and circular financing deals.

title: SoftBank Posts First Loss in Two Years on U.S. Data Center Writedowns
summary: SoftBank Group reported a net loss of about JPY1.1 trillion ($7.1 billion) for its most recent quarter, its first loss in two years. The company attributed the result mainly to charges on power-generation equipment tied to its U.S. AI data-center projects.

title: Nvidia's Nemotron Bright Spot
summary: Booz Allen Hamilton switched from mainly Anthropic models to Nvidia's open-source Nemotron models to run its cybersecurity and defense software, citing significant cost savings, though its developers still mostly use Claude Code to build software. Nemotron accounted for nearly 17% of the roughly 50 trillion tokens processed on Kilo Code in October, up from 8%, and Nvidia's partnership with Palantir is helping it win government users. On OpenRouter, however, Nemotron holds about 4% of tokens and under 1% of spending, while Anthropic leads with 31% of customer spending so far in November.

title: Why HubSpot, Snowflake and Others Are Avoiding AI Spending Caps
summary: As enterprises try to moderate AI costs, they are diverging on whether to impose hard token caps on software engineers, with HubSpot and Snowflake among those avoiding them while companies such as Apple, Microsoft and Disney have restricted spending. Syndio CEO Maria Colacurcio said job candidates at large employers are now negotiating higher or unlimited token budgets and access to the latest models as informal side agreements. Token allowances could become a formal employee benefit if AI prices stay high.

title: NextEra's Takeover of Dominion Faces Mounting Opposition in Virginia
summary: NextEra Energy's proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy, which would create the world's largest retail electric utility, is meeting resistance from Virginia's governor and attorney general. Residents angry over rising electricity prices, an issue that shaped last week's midterms, also oppose the deal. Critics argue it offers too little to customers and could raise costs.

title: Nvidia-Backed Cohere Says IPO Timing Uncertain Despite Surging Revenue
summary: Canadian AI company Cohere said the timing of its planned stock-market listing is uncertain even as its revenue grows rapidly. The WSJ frames the delay as another sign of weakness in the IPO market for AI companies amid recent turbulence in AI stocks.

title: Google to Invest $15 Billion in Malaysia Over Two Years
summary: Google plans to invest $15 billion in new campuses in Malaysia over roughly the next two years. Separately, Alphabet is building a new manufacturing facility in Texas for its drone unit.

title: BT Holds Off on Starlink Direct-to-Device Launch Amid Ukraine Controversy
summary: BT Group CEO Allison Kirkby told the Financial Times that the company's direct-to-device satellite service with Starlink is ready to launch. BT will nonetheless wait until a recent controversy over Starlink's presence in Ukraine subsides before switching it on.

title: Vodafone Upbeat on H1 Despite EUR4.9 Billion German Impairment
summary: Vodafone Group CEO Margherita Della Valle gave a positive outlook on first-half fiscal performance and early progress on a EUR2 billion cost-cutting program. The operator still booked a EUR4.9 billion impairment in Germany, where its business continues to struggle.

title: Amazon and Google Reap Huge Gains on Anthropic Stakes
summary: Anthropic's updated IPO filing shows Amazon's roughly 20% economic stake, from about $18.6 billion invested, would be worth around $258 billion at the midpoint of the proposed price range, though a self-imposed cap limits its holding to 12% of shares. Google's roughly 10% stake, from about $33 billion invested, would be worth about $132 billion. Anthropic has also committed to spend at least $121 billion with Google Cloud through 2033 and at least $110 billion with Amazon's cloud unit through 2036.

title: CoreWeave Finds a Workaround to Capital Constraints—for Now
summary: CoreWeave beat Wall Street's third-quarter revenue expectations and raised its sales guidance, sending shares higher premarket after a slide that had more than halved the stock since August. With borrowing costs elevated, the AI cloud provider is leaning on customer prepayments, collected on about 70% of its deals this year, and launched a new stock-sale program after its CEO said it would not tap unsecured debt markets at current yields. Heard on the Street argues its expansion plans will still depend on cooperative capital markets.

title: OpenAI Revenue Rises to $10 Billion as Heavy Losses Continue
summary: OpenAI told investors its third-quarter revenue rose about 50% from the prior quarter to roughly $10 billion, rebounding from a period of slower growth, while adjusted operating losses edged up to $10.9 billion. The company said paying ChatGPT users reached about 100 million. Rival Anthropic reported $17 billion in third-quarter revenue and a $567 million operating loss.

title: Wachtell Lipton to Lead Nvidia Internal Investigation
summary: Nvidia's board hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to run an independent investigation into whether the company was the target of a foreign espionage effort and into CEO Jensen Huang's conduct. Former federal prosecutor Joon Kim, who joined Wachtell last month, will lead the probe.

title: Jensen Huang Affair Revives Push for Chip Restrictions on Capitol Hill
summary: Lawmakers from both parties said they hope to add three proposed measures tightening exports of AI chips to a stalled defense package, following revelations about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair. The restrictions could cost Nvidia and other semiconductor companies billions of dollars in revenue.

title: Nvidia Scandal Tests the Resilience of the Global AI Boom
summary: The WSJ examines whether the AI investment cycle can keep its momentum while Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, its most prominent champion, is embroiled in a scandal. The piece weighs how much of the industry's narrative of a new industrial revolution rests on Huang personally.

title: Anthropic Founders' Stakes Are Worth $18 Billion Apiece at IPO Price
summary: Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei and Anthropic's five other co-founders each plan to sell about $250 million of stock in the company's IPO later this month. After the sales, each founder would retain a stake worth roughly $18 billion at the offering price.

title: TSMC Approves Up to $1 Billion Investment Plan in Anthropic and OpenAI
summary: TSMC approved investing up to $500 million each in Anthropic, at its IPO price, and in OpenAI, extending its exposure to AI beyond manufacturing the chips. The move was read as a confidence boost for a wobbly AI trade.

title: Alibaba's Chip Unit Files for Hong Kong Listing
summary: T-Head, Alibaba Group's semiconductor unit, filed a confidential application to list on the main board of the Hong Kong stock exchange. The filing adds to a wave of Chinese AI chip companies seeking public capital.

title: Smart-Ring Maker Oura to Buy AI-Native Primary-Care Company for $625 Million
summary: Oura agreed to acquire Counsel Health, an AI-native primary-care provider, for $625 million in cash. The deal broadens Oura's portfolio as the smart-ring maker weighs a public listing.

title: AI Is Testing the Limits of Corporate Governance
summary: Directors at the WSJ Leadership Institute's board summit said static governance cannot keep pace with AI, noting that board materials prepared weeks ahead are often stale by meeting time. They argued boards must become far more technology-literate, overseeing AI's effects on risk, cybersecurity, succession and the redesign of entry-level roles. Several said the conversation has shifted from cutting headcount to using AI to drive strategy.

title: Three States Where the AI Boom Could Slow After the Midterms
summary: Newly elected Democrats in states including Ohio and Texas must decide how to handle trillions of dollars in planned data-center construction. The WSJ identifies three states where the midterm results could slow the AI infrastructure build-out amid local backlash.

title: United Airlines Is Banning AI Bots From Booking Flights
summary: United Airlines is blocking AI agents and automated assistants from booking flights on its behalf, citing data-privacy risks. The carrier also said it does not want to create another intermediary between itself and its customers, an early sign of airlines resisting agentic commerce.

title: Masayoshi Son's Huge Bet on Electrical Turbines Backfires
summary: SoftBank reserved enough gas turbines to generate the output of six Hoover Dams to power planned U.S. AI data centers, a bet that has now cost it billions of dollars. The company wrote off $3.7 billion in non-refundable advance payments for data-center equipment after reviewing its plans.

title: Google Agrees to Privacy Protections in Spirit Airlines Data Sale
summary: Alphabet agreed to additional privacy safeguards to preserve its $10 million purchase of data from bankrupt Spirit Airlines, resolving objections from pilot and flight-attendant unions worried employee files would be used to train AI. Medical, payroll, performance and other employment records are excluded, and an independent agent will verify how the data is used.

title: Palantir CISO Nominated as CISA Director
summary: President Trump nominated Michael LoSapio, Palantir's head of cybersecurity, to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which has lacked a confirmed director since January 2025. LoSapio has no professional government experience, and it is unclear whether the lame-duck Senate will hold confirmation hearings before year-end.

title: Japan Releases $63 Million Emergency Cybersecurity Package
summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi freed up about $63.3 million to strengthen government cybersecurity after a wave of attacks and data breaches at major Japanese companies. The funds will support AI-driven vulnerability testing, stronger defenses and enforcement of cybersecurity laws, with penetration-testing and recovery teams formed this month.

title: Sequoia Capital to Invest in AI Holding Co. Sequence
summary: Sequoia Capital is investing in Sequence, an AI-focused holding company that has been searching for acquisition targets. The deal reflects venture firms' growing interest in roll-up vehicles that buy traditional businesses and overhaul them with AI.

title: Anthropic's PE-Backed Venture, Ode, Pushes to Get Paid for AI Results
summary: Ode, a venture backed by Anthropic and private-equity investors, is pushing clients toward pricing tied to the outcomes its AI delivers rather than seats or usage. The approach tests whether enterprises will pay for measurable results from AI deployments.

title: AI Inference Startups Are Quietly Buying Their Own Chips
summary: Inference startups that built businesses on leasing compute capacity and reselling it are starting to purchase their own AI chips as capacity tightens. The shift raises their capital needs but reduces dependence on cloud providers for scarce GPUs.

title: IBM-Microsoft Survey Finds 13x Agentic AI ROI Gap
summary: An IBM survey of 1,000 C-suite executives conducted with Microsoft found every respondent is increasing agentic AI budgets, but firms with high deployment and strong foundations report 13 times the ROI of laggards. Only 22% report meaningful governance design and operational controls, 22% have an ecosystem strategy, and just 11% have transformationally redesigned workflows.

title: Anthropic Releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, faster upgrades to its top models with per-token prices cut 20%, and Fable 5.2 took first place on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index. Mythos remains limited to vetted security and life-sciences groups, while Fable carries stronger cyber and bio guardrails. Because the new model uses more tokens, maximum-effort tasks cost roughly double those on version 5.1.

title: Reshaping AI Partner Channels for Vendors
summary: McKinsey says partners drive about 60% of technology vendor revenue on average, yet channel programs still follow a traditional SaaS playbook unsuited to AI. More than half of large AI projects rely on partner-led proofs of concept, and McKinsey recommends dedicated AI partner programs, AI-driven channel operations and partners supplying forward-deployed engineers.

title: Telefonica Pushes Potential of 5G in Defence
summary: Telefonica won a contract to supply private 5G to a NATO-mandated defence technology testing centre in Slovakia. The operator expects the project to speed adoption of 5G-supported applications in military settings.

title: Australia to Tighten AI Safety Rules
summary: Australia's government outlined plans to create an AI regulator focused on safety. Companies that breach the new legislation would face significant penalties.
